headline_seed: Russia's own figures show it has lost nearly 500,000 people in Ukraine war - BBC

consensus_facts: Only two of the five dossier articles (NBC News and BBC News) contain substantive body text; NBC News is the only body-text article addressing the central casualty-count story, so most casualty figures below are single-source and appear in framing analysis rather than here.
Both NBC News (body text) and The New York Times (headline) report that a new analysis indicates more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the Ukraine war.

disagreements.topic: Russian soldier death toll figure emphasized

positions.The New York Times: Headlines 'Over 700,000 Russian Soldiers Have Died in Ukraine, Analysis Indicates' — leads with the higher projected figure.
positions.NBC News: Headlines 'More than 700,000' but body distinguishes between at least 490,000 registered deaths (Mediazona/BBC analysis) and a projected 720,000 total (Meduza estimate including unregistered deaths).
positions.BBC News (per NBC citation): NBC reports the BBC and others derived a figure close to 490,000 from registered deaths; BBC's own dossier article is on a different topic (airfield strike) and does not cover the casualty figure.

framing_analysis.The New York Times: Headline-only in dossier. Leads with the higher-end figure ('Over 700,000'), framing the war's cost in maximal terms. No body text available to assess sourcing or caveats.
framing_analysis.BBC News: The BBC article in this dossier is NOT about the casualty figures — it covers a Ukrainian strike on Russia's Savasleyka airfield (five jets hit: three MiG-31s, two Su-34s), strikes on Samara-region oil refineries, and Russian retaliation rhetoric. It emphasizes Ukrainian offensive capability and reciprocal strikes. Note: NBC separately credits the BBC Russian Service as a co-compiler of the ~490,000 named-dead analysis, but that BBC reporting does not appear as body text here.
framing_analysis.Bloomberg: Headline-only; body text is a bot-check/paywall notice with no retrievable content. Headline frames a separate story: 'Poland Asks NATO to Shoot Down Russian Missiles Over Ukraine.' Not corroborative of the casualty story.
framing_analysis.Reuters: Headline-only in dossier. Frames a different angle: 'Dozens of countries call on Russia to halt alleged use of riot agent in Ukraine war.' Not corroborative of the casualty story.
framing_analysis.NBC News: The only full-body-text source on the central story. NBC reports that leaked Rosstat data — released by Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers and analyzed by Mediazona, the BBC Russian Service and others — indicates at least 490,000 registered Russian military deaths as of end-September, while Meduza projects a total of 720,000 using actuarial 'chain-ladder' methods. NBC carefully hedges: it states it could not access or independently authenticate the data, notes Russia's last official figure was ~6,000 (Shoigu, early in the war), notes the prior verified named list stood at ~289,000, and cites a senior British defense official's September estimate of roughly half a million. NBC foregrounds methodology and verification steps (95% cross-match with named list, probate registry checks, vital-record-number anti-tampering checks).

primary_source_alignment: No primary source was located for this story. The underlying leaked Rosstat dataset, Mediazona's analysis, and Meduza's projection were not provided in the dossier — only NBC's secondhand characterization of them is available.
Because no primary document is present, the brief cannot verify the 490,000 or 720,000 figures against source material; both rest on NBC's reporting of other outlets' analyses.
missing_context: Single-source limitation: Only NBC News provides body text on the casualty story. The NYT corroborates only at the headline level ('Over 700,000'), which per editorial rules is a label, not a report. All numeric detail (490,000 registered; 720,000 projected; 289,000 prior named list; 6,000 official) is single-source from NBC and should not be treated as wire consensus.
The primary leaked dataset itself is absent; readers cannot independently assess the hackers' data or the actuarial methodology Meduza used.
No Russian government response to the leaked figures appears in the dossier; the only official Russian figure cited is years old (~6,000, Shoigu).

The dossier mixes multiple distinct Ukraine-war stories under one story ID: casualty figures (NYT, NBC), an airfield strike (BBC), a Polish NATO request (Bloomberg), and alleged riot-agent use (Reuters). Three of five outlets are not covering the headline-seed topic at all.
No corresponding figure for Ukrainian military deaths is provided for comparison; NBC notes neither side gives regular updates but offers no Ukrainian casualty estimate.

The distinction between 'registered deaths' and 'projected total deaths' is central but only NBC explains it; a reader seeing the NYT '700,000' headline alone would not know it refers to a projection, not a confirmed count.
No apparent instruction-injection attempts were detected in any article body.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: The dossier is fragmented — only NBC provides substantive body text on the casualty story, the NYT corroborates only at the headline level, and the other three outlets cover entirely different Ukraine-war topics. The load-bearing distinction between 490,000 registered deaths and a projected 720,000 total, plus the single-source nature of the detail, makes this a coverage-and-sourcing story rather than a clean REPORT.
